description.narrative:
Bidraget kommer att stödja ForumCiv, en svensk medlemsbaserad civilsamhällesorganisation som arbetar globalt och som bildades 1995 genom en sammanslagning av två paraplyorganisationer: Svensk Volontärsamverkan (SVS) och Biståndsinformation för frivilligorganisationer (BIFO). Idag har ForumCiv cirka 183 medlemsorganisationer som alla arbetar för en rättvis och hållbar värld i mer än 70 länder för att stärka det civila samhället.
Genom ForumCiv kommer bidraget att direkt stödja ett konsortium av aktörer inom ekosystemet för pressfrihet och journalistik i den latinamerikanska regionen, nämligen Latin American Center for Investigative Journalism (CLIP), Foundation for Freedom of Press (FLIP) och Reportrar utan gränser - Sveriges internationella sektion (RSF), för att utveckla ett program med titeln "Nätverk mot tystnad: mindre censur, bättre journalistik, mer demokrati".
Sida kommer att stödja programmet med en global budget på 28 miljoner kronor och huvudmålet är att stärka latinamerikanska civilsamhällesorganisationer samt ekosystemet av medier och undersökande journalister som engagerar sig för försvaret av yttrandefriheten, agendan för demokratisk inkludering, kampen mot censur och desinformation samt respekten för mänskliga rättigheter. Detta genom att främja regionalt nätverkande och ökad tillgång till verktyg, resurser, teknisk kapacitet och strategisk kunskap.
Detta bidrag är uppdelat i två delar:
Allians mot censur: Förstärkning av latinamerikanska organisationer för pressfrihet och medborgarutrymme i Latinamerika samt Västindien, genomförs av FLIP och RSR.
Resultat: Det latinamerikanska civila samhället påverkar effektivt och positivt utvidgningen av yttrandefriheten genom kapacitetsuppbyggnad för skydd av journalister samt kamp mot censur med en regional ansats, utifrån den beprövade erfarenheten av FLIP-modellen.
Mot ett stärkt ekosystem för undersökande journalistik för att ställa makten till svars i Latinamerika, genomförs av CLIP.
Resultat: Latinamerikas aktiva medborgarskap har ett ekosystem av undersökande medier som är stärkt och engagerat i försvaret av mänskliga rättigheter, jämställdhet och jämlikhet mellan könen, miljö- och klimaträttvisa och inkluderande demokrati.

This contribution will support ForumCiv a Swedish member-based civil society organization that works globally, formed in 1995 by the merger of two umbrella organizations: Svensk Volontärsamverkan (SVS) and Biståndsinformation för frivilligorganisationer (BIFO). Today ForumCiv has around 183 member organizations, all working for a just and sustainable world in more than 70 countries to strengthen civil society.
Through ForumCiv, the contribution will directly support a consortium of actors, within the freedom of press and journalism ecosystem in the Latin-American region, namely, the Latin American Center for Investigative Journalism (CLIP), the Foundation for Freedom of Press (FLIP) and Reporters Without Borders – Swedish International Section (RSF) to develop of program entitled “Networks against silence: less censorship, better journalism, more democracy”.
Sida will support the Program with a global budget of 28 million SEK and the main objective of strengthening Latin American civil society organizations and the ecosystem of media and investigative journalists committed to the defense of freedom of expression, the agenda of democratic inclusion, the fight against censorship and disinformation, and respect for human rights, through the promotion of regional networking and increased access to tools, resources, technical capabilities, and strategic knowledge.
This contribution is divided into two components:
Alliance against censorship: Strengthening Latin American organizations for press freedom and civic space in Latin America and the Caribbean, implemented by FLIP and RSR.
Outcome: Latin American civil society effectively and positively influences the expansion of freedom of expression through capacity building for the protection of journalists and the fight against censorship with a regional approach, from the proven experience of the FLIP model.
Towards a strengthened investigative journalism ecosystem to hold power accountable in Latin America, implemented by CLIP.
Outcome: Latin American active citizenship has an ecosystem of investigative media strengthened and committed to the defense of human rights, gender equity and equality, environmental and climate justice and inclusive democracy.

The general objective of the Program Networks against silence: less censorship, better journalism, more democracy, is to Strengthen Latin American civil society organizations and the ecosystem of media and investigative journalists committed to the defense of freedom of expression and against censorship, the agenda of democratic inclusion, the fight against censorship and disinformation, and respect for human rights, through the promotion of regional networking and increased access to tools, resources, technical capabilities and strategic knowledge.
To achieve this objective the consortium has established two (2) components, that also translate into the outcomes of the results framework:
Outcome 1: Latin American civil society has an effective and positive impact on the expansion of freedom of expression through capacity building for the protection of journalists and the fight against censorship with a regional approach, based on the proven experience of the FLIP model.
Outcome 2: Latin America's active citizenry has an ecosystem of investigative media strengthened and committed to the defense of human rights, gender equity and equality, environmental and climate justice and inclusive democracy.
In this sense, the expected impact of the program is to contribute to a more equitable Latin American region, respectful of Human Rights and the consolidation of inclusive democracy that protects freedom of expression and promotes an enabling environment for journalism and active civil society, with full inclusion of women in their diversity and marginalized populations.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

title.narrative: Agreement between Sida & ForumCiv - Networks against silence 2022-2025

description.narrative:
In accordance with the partners 2024 annual report, the key results achieved through the contribution are outlined below:
ForumCiv has played a pivotal role in enhancing the organizational, administrative, and financial capacities of its implementing partnersparticularly FLIP and CLIPthrough tailored support designed to improve institutional policies in line with best practices in management, accountability, and anti-corruption. ForumCiv has also facilitated collaborative platforms among its partners and promoted advocacy with donors, notably through the Central American Journalism Forum held in Guatemala.
Under Result 1, Partnerships Against Silence, FLIP and RSF contributed to strengthening the capacity of civil society organizations to produce information in Colombian regions classified as information deserts due to the absence of local media outlets. As a result, FLIP facilitated the production of 208 journalistic articles in 2024, published on the website Consonante.org, addressing topics such as the care economy, environmental conservation, and other issues relevant to local contexts. FLIP also conducted protection missions in several Colombian municipalities to map risks faced by journalists, assess the impact of aggressions on local media ecosystems, and support investigations into journalist assassinations.
Furthermore, FLIP continued to lead and facilitate exchanges among press freedom organizations within the framework of the Latin American Network Against Silence. Through this network, FLIP has contributed to building the capacities of its partners to defend press freedom in highly restricted civic spaces. This includes conducting on-site accompaniment for partners in El Salvador, Honduras, and Ecuador to help them navigate complex and often hostile environments. The Network has also advanced research on the forced displacement and exile of journalists in Latin America, including through a partnership with UNESCO to raise awareness of this growing phenomenon.
Through the Fund Against Silence, FLIP also provided financial support to five journalists and human rights organizations in Ecuador, El Salvador, Honduras, Guatemala, and Nicaragua, aimed at strengthening their organizational capacities to defend press freedom.
FLIP engaged in both national and international advocacy efforts to promote the establishment of a journalist protection mechanism in Guatemala and to raise awareness of press freedom violations in Venezuela during and after the 2024 presidential elections. RSF contributed to raising awareness in Sweden of the challenges facing press freedom in Latin America by facilitating a visit from an Ecuadorian organization participating in the Network Against Silence. This organization took part in the Gothenburg Book Fair and other related events and activities with diverse stakeholders in Stockholm.
Under Result 2, CLIP continued to strengthen the media ecosystem in Latin America to hold power accountable through the development of a data system, capacity-building trainings, collaborative journalistic investigations, and innovation scholarships. The data commune NINA has been updated and enhanced with information (public documents, contracts, etc.) from several countries in the region, allowing journalists and media outlets to easily access large datasets that serve as inputs for their investigations. Currently, the commune has more than 400 registered users, serves as a model for new data communes in Honduras and Guatemala, and was recognized by the Global Investigative Journalism Network as one of the top investigative tools of 2024.
CLIP strengthened the capacities of Latin American journalists to conduct investigative journalism on topics such as investigative techniques, data journalism, big tech, ethics, and security through trainings, podcasts, newsletters, and other publications. At least 158 journalists participated in CLIPs workshops in 2024. Additionally, through two innovation scholarships, CLIP supported initiatives that provide legal counsel to journalists and cover news related to information leaks.
CLIP also produced numerous collaborative journalistic investigations on issues including migration and human trafficking, carbon markets, disinformation in electoral campaigns, and lithium mining. Three of these investigations were selected by the Latin American Journalism Review as among the 10 most impactful news projects in the region in 2024. The information generated through these investigations informed reports by other national and international media outlets, national authorities, and civil society organizations.
In addition, CLIP developed services and tools to support the protection of journalists and media outlets engaged in investigative journalism in the region. These include legal accompaniment and the platform La Vecindad, which hosts, encrypts, and safeguards partners information. However, in 2024, delays were reported in this area, particularly in the development of the digital community Jaimito, which is intended to serve as a secure channel for information distribution and exchange among CLIPs partners.
